title: Episodic rejoin brake and KV coherence escort to prevent rejoin storms
author: Marisol Vega
description: Motivation: we observed multi-region rejoin storms during a flapping infra incident where many nodes reconnected simultaneously and triggered KV cache divergence, transient token floods, and downstream SLO spikes. This PR introduces an "episodic rejoin brake" — a low-latency, tenant-scoped rate limiter that meters node rejoin events and applies exponential backoff windows per-tenant to prevent rapid churn. In parallel it adds a lightweight 'KV coherence escort' that stages in-flight KV snapshots into a transient escrow and performs a quick consistency drain before allowing full traffic on rejoined nodes. Design summary: 1) Rejoin brake is implemented as a token-bucket with a MaxBurst of 3 rejoin tokens and a refill interval configurable by tenant; repeated rejoin attempts consume an exponential-hold token that grows with each suppressed rejoin up to a capped window. 2) KV coherence escort attaches a short-lived 'escrow lease' to a node rejoin; any in-flight KV writes are checkpointed to a per-tenant staging area and reconciled with a fast delta merge before the node is promoted to active. 3) Telemetry: new metrics exported: rejoin_suppressed_total, rejoin_hold_seconds_histogram, kv_escrow_drain_ms, kv_delta_conflicts_total; we added statsd and prometheus labels for tenant_id and region. 4) Controls: new config knobs in runtime/config/rejoin.toml with sane defaults (global holdoff 10s, max_exponential_hold 5m, kv_escrow_timeout 2s) and admin endpoints to query/clear per-tenant hold state. Backwards compatibility and safety: brakes and escort are opt-in via feature flag runtime.rejoin.brake=false->true rollout. When disabled, behavior is unchanged; KV escrow only runs on rejoin flows (no changes to steady-state serving). Testing and rollout: unit tests for token-bucket edge cases and escrow merge conflict resolution included; integration test added to perf-canary harness that simulates 200-node rejoin wave and asserts suppressed rejoin < 5% and no KV divergence; staged rollout is to Canary->region-alpha->global over 48 hours. Checklist: - [x] Token-bucket implementation in runtime core - [x] KV escrow pipeline + reconciliation - [x] Metrics and dashboards (Grafana panel added) - [x] Feature flag + admin API - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Perf canary run and metrics validation - [x] Security review (no new secrets) - [x] Docs note in operations playbook Semantics: this is intended to reduce operational noise and SLO impact during flapping events; it is NOT a replacement for fixing underlying infra instability. Related: ENG-1923 (rejoin telemetry), ENG-2015 (kv-coherence investigations), SUP-8419 (customer incident follow-up).

review_comments: Ethan Chu: Nice isolated impl. Two asks: (1) make the default global holdoff conservative for small tenants, we don't want tiny tenants to be permanently delayed; suggest per-tenant min of 2s. (2) Add a short circuit if KV escrow detects no pending deltas to skip reconciliation.
Marisol Vega: Thanks — addressed both. Added per-tenant min_hold_seconds config and short-circuit path in escrow if delta set is empty, updated tests.
Priya Nair: LGTM overall. Concern: the admin clear endpoint could be abused by automation; can we gate it with a rate limiter and audit log?
Marisol Vega: Added rate limiter on admin clear and ensured every clear emits audit log event with actor and reason. Updated docs.
Liam O'Connor: Can you add a small benchmark to measure escrow drain latency at 10k keys/sec? We should ensure 2s timeout is realistic.
Marisol Vega: Added micro-benchmark in perf-canary recipe and recorded median drain 420ms under 10k keys/sec. Results attached in perf run notes.
Priya Nair: approving after small nits fixed.

release_notes: Introduces an opt-in rejoin rate limiter and KV coherence escort to mitigate multi-node rejoin storms. Default conservative settings should reduce SLO spikes during flapping events.
